translations.text: Commercial Classification of Red Beans
Red bean is one of the important groups of dry legumes that are traded in commercial markets under various names. In foreign standard systems, different types of red beans including
dark red bean, light red bean, and small red bean

are distinguished. These classifications have been formed based on the visual characteristics of the seed and common trade names. Note that these titles relate to United States standard systems and are not necessarily equivalent to official grading in the Iranian market.
Impact of Defects and Seed Appearance on Quality and Price
Seed appearance is one of the most important factors determining the price of dry legumes

. Seeds with fewer defects are placed in higher quality grades and command greater commercial value. Dry legumes are graded based on the extent of defects, with higher quality associated with fewer defects.
Main Grading Criteria
Extent and type of seed defects
Uniformity of seed size and shape
Uniform and glossy seed surface color
Absence of rain-related damage
Rainfall at harvest causes a color change in the seed
and this damage is especially more noticeable in white varieties. Therefore, selecting a dark-seeded variety or Pinto type can reduce the risk of color change due to harvesting.
Fate of Low-Quality Legumes
Legumes that do not meet human consumption quality standards are typically sold as animal feed
and do not enter the food market. These ungraded products or those lacking adequate quality are often directed for this purpose.
Important Points Before Sale
Some buyers announce their quality specifications prior to product delivery.
Obtaining these specifications before delivery is recommended

to avoid discrepancies between buyer expectations and the quality of the produced product. It is recommended to gain information about the sales market and required quality specifications from buyers before planting as well.
Post-Harvest Storage and Packaging
Packaging and storage of dry legumes should be carried out in oxygen-free conditions and away from light
. Oxygen can cause the oils in legume seeds to become rancid, and light quickly fades the color of the seeds. Both factors reduce the visual quality and commercial value of the product.

For long-term storage, using appropriate packaging that prevents oxygen and light penetration is essential. Glass containers are also suitable for small quantities, provided they are stored in a dark place.
Summary of Grading Criteria
Criterion
Description
Commercial Type
Dark red, light red, small red, and other categories
Defect Level
Fewer defects mean higher quality
Seed Appearance
Uniformity of color, shape, and seed size

Rainfall during harvest causes color change
Storage
Oxygen- and light-free to preserve quality
Buyer Specifications
Obtain quality specifications before delivery
Grading Red Bean Product for Sale; Quality, Impurities, and Weight Loss

Red bean is graded based on quality criteria including defect level, seed appearance, and storage conditions. Seed appearance plays a key role in pricing, and seeds with more defects are typically offered as animal feed.
What are the main red bean grading criteria?

The most important red bean grading criteria include the extent of seed defects, appearance and color uniformity, commercial type, and post-harvest storage conditions. Dry legumes are graded based on defects, and the fewer the defects, the higher the quality and price.
How does rainfall during harvest affect the quality of red beans?
Rainfall at harvest causes a color change in the seed. This damage is especially more noticeable in white varieties. To reduce this risk, selecting a dark-seeded variety or Pinto type is recommended.
What happens to legumes that do not meet human consumption quality standards?
Legumes that do not meet human consumption quality standards are typically sold as animal feed and do not enter the food market.
